newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling opens weaker versus dollar.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling opens weaker versus dollar.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling was posted weaker against the dollar on Monday and was poised to decline further on political uncertainty, dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a commercial mean rate of 58.10 against the dollar compared to 57.61 on Friday and at a mean of 98.30 from 97.27 versus the pound.
Commercial banks showed average bids of 59.50 versus the dollar compared to 58.50 at close on Friday.

Dealers said despite central bank intervention on Friday which helped the shilling recoup some of its losses and calmed an extremely jittery market, offshore investors remained cautious and were sitting on the sidelines.
The shilling had depreciated to as low as 61.50 versus the dollar but was adjusted to around 58.50 by close of business.
"Election jitters are likely to put the shilling under pressure," a senior dealer told Reuters.
He said a lot of the pressure was from foreign investors who opted not to roll over investments held in treasury bills.
"They could be in the market (looking for dollars) for about a month or so which means the demand will remain high," a dealer told Reuters.

The intervention on Friday was the largest amount the central bank has had to sell for several years to calm a nervous market. Italso signalled that the bank had more dollars than market demand had anticipated.
Governor Micah Cheserem said on Friday that the bank would stand by on Monday should more demand arise. But there was no early indication from the central bank that there was dollar demand pressure.
The money market remained tight with overnight rates quoted at between 20 and 23 percent unchanged.
